claims.evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claims.claim: The Nsps participate in disrupting host cellular processes and pathways to escape immune recognition and facilitate viral propagation.
claims.source: The Nsps also participate in disrupting host cellular processes and pathways to escape immune recognition and facilitate viral propagation (reviewed in Minkoff and tenOever, 2023; Suryawanshi et al., 2021).
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claims.claim: The maturation step to release the individual Nsp polypeptides is executed by two viral-encoded proteases: Nsp5 and Nsp3.
claims.source: The maturation step to release the individual Nsp polypeptides is executed by two viral-encoded proteases: Nsp5 (also known as Main Protease, MPro/3C-like protease) and Nsp3 (also known as Papain-Like Protease, PLPro) (Narayanan et al., 2022).
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claims.claim: Nsp3 is contained within pp1a and releases itself from the polyprotein through self-cleavage.
claims.source: Nsp3 is contained within pp1a and releases itself from the polyprotein through self-cleavage.
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge about Nsp3 function.

claims.claim: Nsp3 cleaves pp1a at multiple sites to release Nsp1 through Nsp4.
claims.source: Nsp3 also cleaves pp1a at multiple sites to release Nsp1 through Nsp4 (Yan and Wu, 2021).
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claims.claim: The Nsp5 main protease processes pp1b at eleven sites to release itself and Nsp4 to Nsp16.
claims.source: The Nsp5 main protease processes pp1b at eleven sites to release itself and Nsp4 to Nsp16 (Chen et al., 2021).
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claims.claim: Nsp3 and Nsp5 have been found to cleave endogenous host proteins linked to the immune response and cell survival.
claims.source: Besides cleaving viral substrates, Nsp3 and Nsp5 have also been found to cleave endogenous host proteins linked to the immune response and cell survival (Liu et al., 2021; Meyer et al., 2021; Meyers et al., 2021; Moustaqil et al., 2021; Wenzel et al., 2021; Zhang et al., 2021b).
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge supported by multiple citations.

claims.claim: Nsp3 and Nsp5 are essential for viral replication and represent well-characterized drug targets among coronaviruses.
claims.source: Nsp3 and Nsp5 are essential for viral replication and represent well-characterized drug targets among coronaviruses.
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge about coronavirus biology and drug development.

claims.claim: The active component of the antiviral drug Paxlovid is nirmatrelvir, a reversible covalent inhibitor of the Nsp5 main protease.
claims.source: Notably, the active component of the antiviral drug Paxlovid is nirmatrelvir, a reversible covalent inhibitor of the Nsp5 main protease (Owen et al., 2021).
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claims.claim: Paxlovid reduces viral replication and disease severity in patients with COVID-19 by inhibiting Nsp5 proteolytic activity.
claims.source: By inhibiting Nsp5 proteolytic activity, Paxlovid reduces viral replication and disease severity in patients with COVID-19.
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge about Paxlovid's mechanism and clinical effects.

claims.claim: Purification of individual SARS-CoV-2 proteins from human cells identified a potential interaction between a catalytic-inactive version of Nsp5 with human TRMT1.
claims.source: Purification of individual SARS-CoV-2 proteins from human cells have identified a potential interaction between a catalytic-inactive version of Nsp5 with human TRMT1 (Gordon et al., 2020a).
claims.evidence: This is prior work cited from the literature.

claims.claim: TRMT1 interacts with a catalytic-inactive version of Nsp5 encoded by SARS-CoV-1, which is 98.7% similar to SARS-CoV-2.
claims.source: A cross-coronavirus investigation from the same group has extended this observation by finding that TRMT1 interacts with a catalytic-inactive version of Nsp5 encoded by SARS-CoV-1, which is 98.7% similar to SARS-CoV-2 (Gordon et al., 2020b).
claims.evidence: This is prior work cited from the literature.

claims.claim: No detectable interaction was found between TRMT1 and Nsp5 encoded by MERS-CoV, which has 66.8% similarity with SARS-CoV-2.
claims.source: Interestingly, the same study found no detectable interaction between TRMT1 and Nsp5 encoded by MERS-CoV, which has 66.8% similarity with SARS-CoV-2.
claims.evidence: This is prior work cited from the literature.

claims.claim: TRMT1 was identified as a potential interactor with catalytic-inactive Nsp5 using proximity-dependent biotinylation.
claims.source: TRMT1 was also identified as a potential interactor with catalytic-inactive Nsp5 using proximity-dependent biotinylation (Samavarchi-Tehrani et al., 2020).
claims.evidence: This is prior work cited from the literature.

claims.claim: TRMT1 catalyzes the formation of dimethylguanosine (m2,2G) at position 26 in more than half of all human tRNAs.
claims.source: TRMT1 is a tRNA modification enzyme that catalyzes the formation of dimethylguanosine (m2,2G) at position 26 in more than half of all human tRNAs (Dewe et al., 2017; Jonkhout et al., 2021).
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claims.claim: The m2,2G modification is located at a key structural position in tRNAs and is hypothesized to play a role in proper tRNA folding.
claims.source: The m2,2G modification is located at a key structural position in tRNAs and is hypothesized to play a role in proper tRNA folding (Pallan et al., 2008; Steinberg and Cedergren, 1995).
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge and hypothesis supported by citations.

claims.claim: TRMT1-deficient human cells exhibit perturbations in global protein synthesis and decreased proliferation.
claims.source: TRMT1-deficient human cells exhibit perturbations in global protein synthesis and decreased proliferation (Dewe et al., 2017).
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claims.claim: Loss-of-function variants in the TRMT1 gene are the cause of certain types of intellectual disability disorders in humans.
claims.source: Moreover, loss-of-function variants in the TRMT1 gene are the cause of certain types of intellectual disability disorders in humans (Blaesius et al., 2018; Najmabadi et al., 2011; Zhang et al., 2020).
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claims.claim: Changes in TRMT1 activity can impact protein synthesis leading to downstream cellular and biological effects.
claims.source: Thus, changes in TRMT1 activity can impact protein synthesis leading to downstream cellular and biological effects.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on established knowledge about TRMT1 function.

claims.claim: Retroviruses such as HIV use cellular tRNAs as primers for reverse transcription and other viral functions.
claims.source: In one well-known example, retroviruses such as HIV use cellular tRNAs as primers for reverse transcription and other viral functions (reviewed in Jin and Musier-Forsyth, 2019).
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claims.claim: DNA and RNA viruses can impact tRNA synthesis, processing, and charging to modulate infection and pathogenesis.
claims.source: DNA and RNA viruses can also impact tRNA synthesis, processing, and charging to modulate infection and pathogenesis (Dremel et al., 2022; Netzer et al., 2009; Tucker et al., 2020).
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claims.claim: Chikungunya RNA virus infection increases the expression of a human tRNA modification enzyme and alters tRNA modification patterns to favor viral protein expression.
claims.source: In a recent study, Chikungunya RNA virus infection has been shown to increase the expression of a human tRNA modification enzyme and alter tRNA modification patterns to favor viral protein expression (Jungfleisch et al., 2022).
claims.evidence: This is prior work cited from the literature.

claims.claim: SARS-CoV-2 viral particles exhibit an enrichment of specific host tRNAs with distinct modification profiles.
claims.source: Interestingly, SARS-CoV-2 viral particles exhibit an enrichment of specific host tRNAs with distinct modification profiles (Peña et al., 2022).
claims.evidence: This is prior work cited from the literature.

claims.claim: Analysis of RNA extracted from human nose swabs identified tRNA profiles and modification signatures associated with mild versus severe COVID-19.
claims.source: Moreover, analysis of RNA extracted from human nose swabs have identified tRNA profiles and modification signatures associated with mild versus severe COVID-19 (Katanski et al., 2022).
claims.evidence: This is prior work cited from the literature.

claims.claim: MRC-5 cells infected with SARS-CoV-2 exhibited a ~30% reduction in TRMT1 levels at 24- and 48 hr post-infection compared to mock-infected cells.
claims.source: In multiple independent replicates, MRC-5 cells infected with SARS-CoV-2 exhibited a ~30% reduction in TRMT1 levels at 24- and 48 hr post-infection compared to mock-infected cells (Figure 1B).
claims.evidence: The manuscript presents quantified immunoblot data showing this reduction.

claims.claim: m2,2G levels were decreased by ~15% at 48 hr post-infection in SARS-CoV-2-infected cells compared to mock-infected cells.
claims.source: While m2,2G levels did not exhibit a significant change between mock-infected and SARS-CoV-2-infected cells at 24 hr post-infection, m2,2G levels were decreased by ~15% at 48 hr post-infection in multiple biological replicates (Figure 1C).
claims.evidence: The manuscript presents mass spectrometry data showing this decrease.

claims.claim: More than half of all tested RNA modifications exhibited a decrease in SARS-CoV-2-infected cells compared to mock-infected cells at 24 hr post-infection.
claims.source: In addition to m2,2G, more than half of all tested RNA modifications exhibited a decrease in SARS-CoV-2-infected cells compared to mock-infected cells at 24 hr post-infection (Figure 1D).
claims.evidence: The manuscript presents mass spectrometry data showing changes in multiple RNA modifications.

claims.claim: At 48 hr post-infection with SARS-CoV-2, most of the tested RNA modifications exhibited a decrease in levels compared to mock-infected cells.
claims.source: At 48 hr post-infection with SARS-CoV-2, most of the tested RNA modifications exhibited a decrease in levels compared to mock-infected cells.
claims.evidence: The manuscript presents mass spectrometry data showing this trend.

claims.claim: Human TRMT1 contains an eight amino acid residue sequence between the methyltransferase domain and zinc-finger motif matching the consensus sequence of Nsp5 cleavage sites in SARS-CoV-2 polyproteins.
claims.source: Examination of the primary structure of human TRMT1 revealed an eight amino acid residue sequence between the methyltransferase domain and zinc-finger motif matching the consensus sequence of Nsp5 cleavage sites in SARS-CoV-2 polyproteins (Figure 2A and B).
claims.evidence: The manuscript presents sequence analysis showing this match.

claims.claim: The putative cleavage site in TRMT1 includes a glutamine (Q) residue conserved at the fourth position that is found in all Nsp5 cleavage sites of SARS-CoV-2 polyproteins.
claims.source: The putative cleavage site in TRMT1 includes a glutamine (Q) residue conserved at the fourth position that is found in all Nsp5 cleavage sites of SARS-CoV-2 polyproteins (Figure 2B).
claims.evidence: The manuscript presents sequence analysis showing this conservation.

claims.claim: The putative Nsp5 cleavage site in TRMT1 is expected to lie in an unstructured linker region exposed on the surface of TRMT1 based on Alpha Fold prediction.
claims.source: Based upon a predicted tertiary structure of TRMT1 using Alpha Fold (Jumper et al., 2021; Varadi et al., 2022), this putative Nsp5 cleavage site is expected to lie in an unstructured linker region exposed on the surface of TRMT1 (Figure 2C).
claims.evidence: The manuscript presents structural prediction data.

claims.claim: Endogenous TRMT1 was enriched in the purification with Nsp5-C145A.
claims.source: In contrast, endogenous TRMT1 was enriched in the purification with Nsp5-C145A (Figure 2D, TRMT1 high exposure, lane 9).
claims.evidence: The manuscript presents protein purification data showing this enrichment.

claims.claim: TRMT1-FLAG was detected specifically in the Nsp5-C145A purification compared to the control or Nsp5 purifications.
claims.source: TRMT1-FLAG was also detected specifically in the Nsp5-C145A purification compared to the control or Nsp5 purifications (Figure 2D, compare lanes 10 and 11 to lane 12).
claims.evidence: The manuscript presents protein purification data showing this specific detection.

claims.claim: Nsp5 can interact with TRMT1 when Nsp5 is in the catalytic-inactive form.
claims.source: These results provide evidence that Nsp5 can interact with TRMT1 when Nsp5 is in the catalytic-inactive form.
claims.evidence: This is an inference from the purification data showing interaction with Nsp5-C145A.

claims.claim: Cleavage after amino acid residue 530 of TRMT1 is predicted to result in an N-terminal fragment of 58 kDa and a C-terminal fragment of 14 kDa.
claims.source: Cleavage after amino acid residue 530 of TRMT1 is predicted to result in an N-terminal fragment of 58 kDa and a C-terminal fragment of 14 kDa.
claims.evidence: This is a calculation based on the predicted cleavage site and protein sequence.

claims.claim: Lysates prepared from human cells expressing Nsp5 exhibited an additional band migrating below the non-specific band that matches the predicted size of the N-terminal TRMT1 fragment.
claims.source: However, lysates prepared from human cells expressing Nsp5 exhibited an additional band migrating below the non-specific band that matches the predicted size of the N-terminal TRMT1 fragment (Figure 3B, TRMT1, lanes 4–6, arrow).
claims.evidence: The manuscript presents immunoblot data showing this band.

claims.claim: The putative N-terminal TRMT1 fragment was detectable at 24 hr post-transfection with the Nsp5-expression plasmid, increased at 48 hr, and remained detectable at 72 hr post-transfection.
claims.source: The putative N-terminal TRMT1 fragment was detectable at 24 hr post-transfection with the Nsp5-expression plasmid, increased at 48 hr, and remained detectable at 72 hr post-transfection (Figure 3B).
claims.evidence: The manuscript presents time-course immunoblot data.

claims.claim: The N-terminal TRMT1 fragment was not detected above the background signal in human cells expressing the proteolytically inactive Nsp5-C145A mutant.
claims.source: In contrast, the N-terminal TRMT1 fragment was not detected above the background signal in human cells expressing the proteolytically inactive Nsp5-C145A mutant (Figure 3B, TRMT1, lanes 7–9, quantified in 3 C).
claims.evidence: The manuscript presents immunoblot data showing absence of cleavage with Nsp5-C145A.

claims.claim: A ~20 kDa product matching the expected molecular weight of a FLAG-tagged C-terminal TRMT1 cleavage product was detected in the lysate of human cells expressing Nsp5 but not vector alone or Nsp5-C145A.
claims.source: In addition, using an antibody against the FLAG tag, we could detect a ~20 kDa product matching the expected molecular weight of a FLAG-tagged C-terminal TRMT1 cleavage product in the lysate of human cells expressing Nsp5 but not vector alone or Nsp5-C145A (Figure 4A, FLAG, arrowhead).
claims.evidence: The manuscript presents immunoblot data showing the C-terminal fragment.

claims.claim: SARS-CoV-2 Nsp5 cleaves at the predicted cleavage site in TRMT1 leading to N- and C-terminal fragments in human cells.
claims.source: These data provide evidence that SARS-CoV-2 Nsp5 cleaves at the predicted cleavage site in TRMT1 leading to N- and C-terminal fragments in human cells.
claims.evidence: This is an inference from the detection of both N- and C-terminal fragments.

claims.claim: All Nsp5 cleavage sites in SARS-CoV-1 and SARS-CoV-2 polyproteins contain a glutamine residue at position four.
claims.source: All Nsp5 cleavage sites in SARS-CoV-1 and SARS-CoV-2 polyproteins contain a glutamine residue at position four (Figure 2B; Grum-Tokars et al., 2008; Jin et al., 2022; Lee et al., 2022).
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations and sequence analysis.

claims.claim: Mutation of the glutamine to asparagine is sufficient to abolish recognition and cleavage by Nsp5 from SARS-CoV-1 or SARS-CoV-2.
claims.source: Mutation of the glutamine to asparagine is sufficient to abolish recognition and cleavage by Nsp5 from SARS-CoV-1 or SARS-CoV-2 (Heilmann et al., 2022; Muramatsu et al., 2013).
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claims.claim: The appearance of the N- or C-terminal TRMT1 cleavage fragments was barely detectable when the TRMT1-Q530N mutant was co-expressed with Nsp5.
claims.source: In contrast to wild-type TRMT1, the appearance of the N- or C-terminal TRMT1 cleavage fragments was barely detectable when the TRMT1-Q530N mutant was co-expressed with Nsp5 (Figure 4C, lane 8, Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
claims.evidence: The manuscript presents immunoblot data showing lack of cleavage with Q530N mutation.

claims.claim: TRMT1 can be recognized and cleaved by Nsp5 in human cells with cleavage requiring a sequence that matches Nsp5 cleavage sites in SARS-CoV-2 polyproteins.
claims.source: Altogether, these results demonstrate that TRMT1 can be recognized and cleaved by Nsp5 in human cells with cleavage requiring a sequence that matches Nsp5 cleavage sites in SARS-CoV-2 polyproteins.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the mutagenesis and cleavage experiments.

claims.claim: TRMT1 exhibits a stable interaction with rRNAs and substrate tRNAs that are targets for m2,2G modification.
claims.source: We have previously shown that TRMT1 exhibits a stable interaction with rRNAs and substrate tRNAs that are targets for m2,2G modification (Dewe et al., 2017; Zhang et al., 2020).
claims.evidence: This is prior work from the authors' lab supported by citations.

claims.claim: The purification of full-length TRMT1 resulted in the enrichment of rRNA and tRNAs compared to the control purification from vector-transfected cells.
claims.source: As expected, the purification of full-length TRMT1 resulted in the enrichment of rRNA and tRNAs compared to the control purification from vector-transfected cells (Figure 5C, compare lane 6 to lane 7).
claims.evidence: The manuscript presents RNA purification data showing this enrichment.

claims.claim: The Q530N variant of TRMT1 exhibited comparable binding of tRNAs as full-length TRMT1.
claims.source: The Q530N variant of TRMT1 also exhibited comparable binding of tRNAs as full-length TRMT1 (Figure 5C, lane 10).
claims.evidence: The manuscript presents RNA purification data showing comparable binding.

claims.claim: No detectable enrichment of rRNA or tRNA was detected for the N-terminal TRMT1 fragment.
claims.source: In contrast, no detectable enrichment of rRNA or tRNA was detected for the N-terminal TRMT1 fragment (Figure 5C, lane 8).
claims.evidence: The manuscript presents RNA purification data showing lack of enrichment.

claims.claim: The N-terminal TRMT1 cleavage fragment appears to be insufficient for binding tRNA while the C-terminal fragment containing the Zn-finger motif is sufficient for binding to tRNAs.
claims.source: Thus, the N-terminal TRMT1 cleavage fragment appears to be insufficient for binding tRNA while the C-terminal fragment containing the Zn-finger motif is sufficient for binding to tRNAs.
claims.evidence: This is an inference from the RNA binding data.

claims.claim: Re‐expression of full-length TRMT1 or TRMT1-Q530N in the TRMT1‐KO cell line was able to restore m2,2G formation in both tRNA-Met-CAU and mt-tRNA-Ile-UAU.
claims.source: Re‐expression of full-length TRMT1 or TRMT1-Q530N in the TRMT1‐KO cell line was able to restore m2,2G formation in both tRNA-Met-CAU and mt-tRNA-Ile-UAU (Figure 5E, lanes 7 and 9).
claims.evidence: The manuscript presents primer extension data showing rescue of modification.

claims.claim: Neither the N- nor C-terminal TRMT1 fragment was able to restore m2,2G formation in the tRNAs of the TRMT1‐KO cell line.
claims.source: However, neither the N- nor C-terminal TRMT1 fragment was able to restore m2,2G formation in the tRNAs of the TRMT1‐KO cell line (Figure 5E, lanes 8 and 10).
claims.evidence: The manuscript presents primer extension data showing lack of rescue.

claims.claim: Cleavage of TRMT1 by Nsp5 leads to protein fragments that are inactive for tRNA modification activity.
claims.source: These results indicate that cleavage of TRMT1 by Nsp5 leads to protein fragments that are inactive for tRNA modification activity.
claims.evidence: This is an inference from the functional rescue experiments.

claims.claim: Full-length TRMT1-GFP exhibited cytoplasmic localization along with a punctate signal in the nucleus.
claims.source: Full-length TRMT1-GFP exhibited cytoplasmic localization along with a punctate signal in the nucleus (Figure 5—figure supplement 1, TRMT1-WT, GFP).
claims.evidence: The manuscript presents microscopy data showing this localization pattern.

claims.claim: The fluorescence signal for TRMT1 in the cytoplasm overlapped partially with the RFP-tagged mitochondrial marker.
claims.source: The fluorescence signal for TRMT1 in the cytoplasm overlapped partially with the RFP-tagged mitochondrial marker (Figure 5—figure supplement 1, Merge, yellow signal).
claims.evidence: The manuscript presents microscopy data showing this overlap.

claims.claim: The N-terminal TRMT1 fragment exhibited primarily cytoplasmic localization with a greatly reduced signal in the nucleus.
claims.source: The N-terminal TRMT1 fragment exhibited primarily cytoplasmic localization with a greatly reduced signal in the nucleus, consistent with a lack of the nuclear localization signal at the C-terminus (Figure 5—figure supplement 1, TRMT1 N-term, GFP, merge).
claims.evidence: The manuscript presents microscopy data showing this localization pattern.

claims.claim: The C-terminal TRMT1 fragment displayed primarily nuclear localization with very little signal in the cytoplasm.
claims.source: In contrast to the N-terminal TRMT1 fragment, the C-terminal TRMT1 fragment displayed primarily nuclear localization with very little signal in the cytoplasm (Figure 5—figure supplement 1, TRMT1 C-term, GFP, merge).
claims.evidence: The manuscript presents microscopy data showing this localization pattern.

claims.claim: TRMT1 in the cytoplasm is the likely target of Nsp5 cleavage with the cleavage fragments displaying altered localization compared to full-length TRMT1.
claims.source: These results suggest that TRMT1 in the cytoplasm is the likely target of Nsp5 cleavage with the cleavage fragments displaying altered localization compared to full-length TRMT1.
claims.evidence: This is an inference from the localization data.

claims.claim: TRMT1 protein levels decreased in the TRMT1-KO cell lines expressing TRMT1-WT after infection with SARS-CoV-2 compared to mock-infection.
claims.source: Compared to mock-infection, TRMT1 protein levels decreased in the TRMT1-KO cell lines expressing TRMT1-WT after infection with SARS-CoV-2 (Figure 7A, lanes 1–3; quantified in 7B).
claims.evidence: The manuscript presents immunoblot data showing this decrease.

claims.claim: The level of TRMT1 was not appreciably changed in the TRMT1-KO cell line expressing TRMT1-Q530N after infection with SARS-CoV-2.
claims.source: Notably, the level of TRMT1 was not appreciably changed in the TRMT1-KO cell line expressing TRMT1-Q530N after infection with SARS-CoV-2 (Figure 7A, lanes 4–6; quantified in 7 C).
claims.evidence: The manuscript presents immunoblot data showing stable TRMT1-Q530N levels.

claims.claim: The decrease in endogenous TRMT1 levels after SARS-CoV-2 infection is due to cleavage of TRMT1 by Nsp5.
claims.source: These results provide evidence that the decrease in endogenous TRMT1 levels after SARS-CoV-2 infection is due to cleavage of TRMT1 by Nsp5.
claims.evidence: This is an inference from the comparison of TRMT1-WT and TRMT1-Q530N stability during infection.

claims.claim: TRMT1-KO cells exhibited a ~three to fourfold reduction in viral RNA compared to control cells infected at the same MOI.
claims.source: Notably, TRMT1-KO cells exhibited a ~three to fourfold reduction in viral RNA compared to control cells infected at the same MOI (Figure 6E and F).
claims.evidence: The manuscript presents qRT-PCR data showing this reduction.

claims.claim: Expression of TRMT1 is necessary for efficient SARS-CoV-2 replication in human cells.
claims.source: These results suggest that expression of TRMT1 is necessary for efficient SARS-CoV-2 replication in human cells.
claims.evidence: This is an inference from the reduced viral RNA in TRMT1-KO cells.

claims.claim: TRMT1-KO cell lines re-expressing TRMT1 exhibited higher viral RNA production relative to the TRMT1-KO+vector cell line that was comparable to the control-WT cells.
claims.source: TRMT1-KO cell lines re-expressing TRMT1 exhibited higher viral RNA production relative to the TRMT1-KO+vector cell line that was comparable to the control-WT cells (Figure 7D, compare KO +vec to KO +WT).
claims.evidence: The manuscript presents qRT-PCR data showing rescue of viral replication.

claims.claim: The TRMT1-KO cell line expressing TRMT1-Q530N exhibited a higher level of viral RNA production compared to the TRMT1-KO cell line expressing TRMT1-WT at higher MOI.
claims.source: Notably, the TRMT1-KO cell line expressing TRMT1-Q530N exhibited a higher level of viral RNA production compared to the TRMT1-KO cell line expressing TRMT1-WT at higher MOI (Figure 7, KO +Q530 N).
claims.evidence: The manuscript presents qRT-PCR data showing enhanced replication with non-cleavable TRMT1.

claims.claim: The presence or absence of TRMT1 impacts SARS-CoV-2 RNA production in human 293T cells.
claims.source: Since the presence or absence of TRMT1 appears to impact SARS-CoV-2 RNA production in human 293T cells, we tested if this phenomenon could alter viral particle production.
claims.evidence: This is an inference from the viral RNA quantification experiments.

claims.claim: The supernatant from infected TRMT1-KO cells exhibited reduced titer and slightly lower infectivity when compared to viral particles produced from control-WT cells.
claims.source: Consistent with the reduced levels of viral RNA in TRMT1-KO cells infected with SARS-CoV-2, the supernatant from infected TRMT1-KO cells exhibited reduced titer and slightly lower infectivity when compared to viral particles produced from control-WT cells (Figure 8, control-WT versus TRMT1-KO).
claims.evidence: The manuscript presents viral titer and infectivity data.

claims.claim: Re-expression of TRMT1 in the TRMT1-KO cells partially restored viral titer at the lower MOI and increased infectivity compared to supernatants from TRMT1-KO cell lines.
claims.source: Re-expression of TRMT1 in the TRMT1-KO cells partially restored viral titer at the lower MOI and increased infectivity compared to supernatants from TRMT1-KO cell lines (Figure 8, TRMT1-KO+vec versus TRMT1-KO+WT).
claims.evidence: The manuscript presents viral titer and infectivity data showing partial rescue.

claims.claim: The expression of the non-cleavable TRMT1-Q530N variant in TRMT1-KO cells promoted an increase of viral titer as well as infectivity compared to expression of wild-type TRMT1.
claims.source: Interestingly, the expression of the non-cleavable TRMT1-Q530N variant in TRMT1-KO cells promoted an increase of viral titer as well as infectivity compared to expression of wild-type TRMT1 (Figure 8, TRMT1-KO+WT versus TRMT1-KO+Q530 N).
claims.evidence: The manuscript presents viral titer and infectivity data showing enhanced production with non-cleavable TRMT1.

claims.claim: TRMT1 expression plays a role in virus production and the generation of optimally infectious SARS-CoV-2 particles.
claims.source: Altogether, these observations suggest an unexpected role for TRMT1 expression in virus production and the generation of optimally infectious SARS-CoV-2 particles.
claims.evidence: This is an inference from the viral titer and infectivity experiments.

claims.claim: TRMT1 is an endogenous cleavage target of the SARS-CoV-2 main protease.
claims.source: Here, we demonstrate that TRMT1 tRNA modification enzyme is an endogenous cleavage target of the SARS-CoV-2 main protease.
claims.evidence: This is the main conclusion of the manuscript supported by multiple experiments.

claims.claim: D'Oliviera et al. have determined the structural basis for recognition of TRMT1 by the SARS-CoV-2 main protease, which has revealed a distinct binding mode for certain substrates of the main protease, including TRMT1.
claims.source: D'Oliviera et al. have determined the structural basis for recognition of TRMT1 by the SARS-CoV-2 main protease, which has revealed a distinct binding mode for certain substrates of the main protease, including TRMT1.
claims.evidence: This is a reference to concurrent work by another group.

claims.claim: The study by D'Oliviera et al. and the current manuscript provide independent corroboration of each other's main conclusion that TRMT1 is recognized and cleaved by the SARS-CoV-2 main protease in a sequence-specific manner.
claims.source: Together, our study and the investigation by D'Oliviera et al. provide independent corroboration of each other's main conclusion that TRMT1 is recognized and cleaved by the SARS-CoV-2 main protease in a sequence-specific manner.
claims.evidence: This is a statement about the convergence of findings from two independent studies.

claims.claim: An independent study by Lu and Zhou, 2023 has further confirmed the findings that the SARS-CoV-2 main protease can cleave TRMT1.
claims.source: Moreover, after our manuscript and the manuscript by D'Oliviera et al. were deposited on BioRxiv, an independent study by Lu and Zhou, 2023 has further confirmed our findings that the SARS-CoV-2 main protease can cleave TRMT1.
claims.evidence: This is a reference to additional confirming work by another group.

claims.claim: TRMT1 could represent a coincidental substrate of Nsp5 during SARS-CoV-2 infection due to the presence of a sequence matching the cleavage site of SARS-CoV-2 polyproteins.
claims.source: TRMT1 could represent a coincidental substrate of Nsp5 during SARS-CoV-2 infection due to the presence of a sequence matching the cleavage site of SARS-CoV-2 polyproteins.
claims.evidence: This is speculation about the nature of TRMT1 as an Nsp5 substrate.

claims.claim: Nsp5 could have access mainly to newly synthesized TRMT1 in the cytoplasm since the majority of TRMT1 exhibits steady-state localization to the nucleus and mitochondria.
claims.source: Since the majority of TRMT1 exhibits steady-state localization to the nucleus and mitochondria of multiple human cell types (Dewe et al., 2017), Nsp5 could have access mainly to newly synthesized TRMT1 in the cytoplasm.
claims.evidence: This is speculation based on known TRMT1 localization patterns.

claims.claim: The effect of SARS-CoV-2 infection on TRMT1 levels could depend on the concentration of TRMT1, half-life of TRMT1, and/or amount of Nsp5 expression in the infected cell.
claims.source: Moreover, the effect of SARS-CoV-2 infection on TRMT1 levels could depend on the concentration of TRMT1, half-life of TRMT1, and/or amount of Nsp5 expression in the infected cell.
claims.evidence: This is speculation about factors affecting TRMT1 cleavage during infection.

claims.claim: A subset of proteomic studies has found decreased TRMT1 protein levels in SARS-CoV-2-infected human cells as well as in post-mortem tissue samples from deceased COVID-19 patients.
claims.source: Consistent with our results, a subset of proteomic studies has found decreased TRMT1 protein levels in SARS-CoV-2-infected human cells as well as in post-mortem tissue samples from deceased COVID-19 patients (Bojkova et al., 2020; Nie et al., 2021).
claims.evidence: This is prior work cited from the literature that supports the current findings.

claims.claim: SARS-CoV-2 infection could impact TRMT1 protein levels and tRNA modification patterns within the cells of an infected individual.
claims.source: These findings suggest that SARS-CoV-2 infection could impact TRMT1 protein levels and tRNA modification patterns within the cells of an infected individual.

results.result: SARS-CoV-2 Nsp5 interacts with human TRMT1. The authors identify a putative Nsp5 cleavage site in TRMT1 matching the consensus sequence of viral polyprotein cleavage sites, including a conserved glutamine at position 4. This site is predicted to be surface-exposed. Co-purification experiments show that catalytically inactive Nsp5-C145A, but not wild-type Nsp5, enriches endogenous and FLAG-tagged TRMT1.
results.evaluation: Claims C44-C46 provide bioinformatic evidence for a putative cleavage site, while C47-C48 demonstrate specific interaction between Nsp5-C145A and TRMT1 through co-purification experiments. The use of catalytically inactive Nsp5 is appropriate for detecting substrate interactions. The convergent evidence from sequence analysis and biochemical interaction supports this result.

results.result: Nsp5 cleaves TRMT1 at a specific site matching viral polyprotein cleavage consensus sequences. Expression of wild-type Nsp5, but not catalytically inactive Nsp5-C145A, produces N-terminal (~58 kDa) and C-terminal (~20 kDa) TRMT1 fragments detectable by immunoblotting. Mutation of the conserved glutamine at position 530 to asparagine (Q530N) abolishes cleavage.
results.evaluation: Claims C51-C53 and C55 provide direct experimental evidence of TRMT1 cleavage fragments appearing only with wild-type Nsp5. The Q530N mutation experiment (C59) provides strong evidence for site-specificity by abolishing cleavage. The fragments match predicted sizes (C50), and the requirement for glutamine at position 4 is consistent with established Nsp5 specificity (C57-C58). Multiple independent experiments support this conclusion.

results.result: SARS-CoV-2 infection reduces cellular TRMT1 protein levels. MRC-5 cells infected with SARS-CoV-2 show ~30% reduction in TRMT1 at 24 and 48 hours post-infection. At high MOI (5.0), TRMT1 levels are reduced to near-background. The non-cleavable TRMT1-Q530N mutant is resistant to this reduction during infection, indicating that cleavage by Nsp5 is responsible.
results.evaluation: Claims C40 and C118 provide quantified immunoblot data showing TRMT1 reduction in infected cells. The critical experiment comparing TRMT1-WT and TRMT1-Q530N stability during infection (C75-C76) provides strong evidence that Nsp5 cleavage is responsible for TRMT1 reduction. Multiple cell types and MOIs were tested, strengthening the conclusion.

results.result: SARS-CoV-2 infection reduces TRMT1-catalyzed m2,2G tRNA modifications and other RNA modifications. m2,2G levels decreased by ~15% at 48 hours post-infection. More than half of tested RNA modifications showed decreases at 24 hours, with most modifications decreased at 48 hours post-infection.
results.evaluation: Claims C41-C43 present mass spectrometry data showing reduction in m2,2G and other RNA modifications. The data are quantified and include biological replicates. However, the broad reduction in multiple RNA modifications (C42-C43) suggests effects beyond TRMT1 cleavage alone, which the authors acknowledge. The m2,2G reduction is modest (~15%) and only significant at 48 hours, which is consistent with partial TRMT1 depletion rather than complete loss.

results.result: TRMT1 cleavage fragments exhibit altered RNA binding properties. The N-terminal fragment shows no detectable enrichment of rRNA or tRNA, while the C-terminal fragment containing the zinc finger motif retains tRNA binding comparable to full-length TRMT1. The non-cleavable Q530N mutant binds RNA normally.
results.evaluation: Claims C62-C64 provide RNA co-purification data showing differential binding by TRMT1 fragments. The C-terminal fragment retains tRNA binding while the N-terminal fragment does not, which is consistent with the zinc finger motif being in the C-terminal region. The Q530N control (C63) demonstrates that the mutation itself doesn't affect RNA binding. The experimental approach is appropriate for assessing RNA-protein interactions.

results.result: TRMT1 cleavage fragments are catalytically inactive and cannot rescue tRNA modification in TRMT1-deficient cells. Full-length TRMT1 and TRMT1-Q530N restore m2,2G modification in both nuclear and mitochondrial tRNAs in TRMT1-KO cells, but neither N-terminal nor C-terminal fragments can rescue modification.
results.evaluation: Claims C67-C68 present primer extension assays showing functional rescue by full-length TRMT1 but not by cleavage fragments. The use of TRMT1-KO cells as a null background is appropriate. The Q530N mutant serves as a control showing that the mutation doesn't affect catalytic activity. The inability of either fragment to rescue activity is consistent with both domains being required for function.

results.result: TRMT1 is required for efficient SARS-CoV-2 replication. TRMT1-KO cells show 3-4 fold reduction in viral RNA compared to wild-type cells. Re-expression of TRMT1 rescues viral replication to wild-type levels. Notably, expression of non-cleavable TRMT1-Q530N results in higher viral RNA production than wild-type TRMT1 at higher MOI.
results.evaluation: Claims C78 and C80 provide qRT-PCR data showing reduced viral RNA in TRMT1-KO cells and rescue by TRMT1 re-expression. The genetic complementation experiment (C80) is critical for establishing causality. The enhanced replication with TRMT1-Q530N (C81) is particularly interesting and suggests that TRMT1 cleavage may limit viral replication. Multiple MOIs were tested, strengthening the conclusions.

results.result: TRMT1 expression affects SARS-CoV-2 particle production and infectivity. Viral particles from TRMT1-KO cells show reduced titer and slightly lower infectivity. Re-expression of TRMT1 partially restores titer and increases infectivity. Expression of non-cleavable TRMT1-Q530N further enhances both viral titer and infectivity compared to wild-type TRMT1.
results.evaluation: Claims C83-C85 present viral titer and infectivity measurements showing effects of TRMT1 on virus production. The TCID50 assay is appropriate for measuring infectious virus. The enhanced infectivity with TRMT1-Q530N (C85) is consistent with the viral RNA data and suggests that preventing TRMT1 cleavage benefits the virus. However, the mechanism remains unclear and requires further investigation.

results.result: TRMT1 cleavage fragments exhibit altered subcellular localization. Full-length TRMT1 shows cytoplasmic and nuclear localization with partial mitochondrial overlap. The N-terminal fragment is primarily cytoplasmic with reduced nuclear signal, while the C-terminal fragment is predominantly nuclear.
results.evaluation: Claims C70-C73 present microscopy data showing distinct localization patterns for full-length TRMT1 and its fragments. The altered localization is consistent with the C-terminal fragment containing the nuclear localization signal. The cytoplasmic localization of full-length TRMT1 supports the inference that cytoplasmic TRMT1 is the target of Nsp5 cleavage (C74). The use of mitochondrial and nuclear markers provides appropriate controls.

results.result: The authors conclude that Nsp5-dependent cleavage of TRMT1 and perturbation of tRNA modification patterns contribute to SARS-CoV-2 cellular pathogenesis. They suggest this could affect protein synthesis, cellular proliferation, metabolism, and potentially contribute to COVID-19 disease outcomes.
results.evaluation: While the experimental data clearly demonstrate TRMT1 cleavage by Nsp5 (C87) and effects on tRNA modifications (C95), the connection to cellular pathogenesis (C11) and disease outcomes (C98) is largely speculative. The modest reduction in m2,2G levels (~15%) and the observation that TRMT1-KO cells actually show reduced viral replication complicate the pathogenesis narrative. Claims C97-C98 are explicitly speculative. More direct evidence linking TRMT1 cleavage to cellular dysfunction would be needed to fully support this conclusion.

results.result: The authors note that concurrent and subsequent independent studies by D'Oliviera et al. and Lu and Zhou have corroborated the finding that TRMT1 is cleaved by SARS-CoV-2 main protease, with D'Oliviera et al. providing structural insights into the recognition mechanism.
results.evaluation: Claims C88-C90 accurately reference concurrent work that independently validates the main finding. The convergence of multiple independent studies strengthens confidence in the core result. This is appropriately presented as corroborating evidence rather than as part of the primary results.

results.result: The authors speculate on multiple possible mechanisms and biological significance of TRMT1 cleavage, including: coincidental targeting due to sequence similarity, effects on translation machinery, potential modification of viral RNAs, tRNA packaging into viral particles, and possible self-limitation of viral replication.
results.evaluation: These claims (C91-C93, C100-C102, C105, C107, C112-C117) are explicitly speculative and presented as such by the authors. While some speculation is supported by citations to related phenomena in other systems, none of these mechanisms are directly tested in this manuscript. The speculation is reasonable given the data but remains unvalidated. Some hypotheses (e.g., C112 about self-limitation) seem inconsistent with the observation that TRMT1-Q530N enhances viral replication.

results.result: SARS-CoV-2 infection causes widespread changes in RNA modifications beyond m2,2G, affecting tRNA, rRNA, snRNA, and mRNA. This suggests that coronavirus infection may alter the levels or activity of multiple RNA modification enzymes in addition to TRMT1.
results.evaluation: Claim C109 presents mass spectrometry data showing broad changes in RNA modifications during infection. The inference that multiple enzymes may be affected (C110) is reasonable given the breadth of changes observed. This is supported by prior knowledge that RNA modification profiles change in response to cellular stress (C111). However, the mechanisms underlying these broad changes are not investigated in this study.

results.result: SARS-CoV-2 infection reduces TRMT1 protein levels in human cells. MRC-5 cells showed ~30% reduction at 24 and 48 hr post-infection, while 293T cells at high MOI (5.0) showed dramatic reduction to near-knockout levels.
results.evaluation: Reviewer 2 notes 'the reduction of bulk TRMT1 levels is minor during infection of MRC5 cells with SARS-CoV-2 (Fig 1)' and questions whether this agrees with the more dramatic reduction in m2,2G levels. Reviewer 1 acknowledges the data but notes 'only a minority of TRMT1 undergoes cleavage during infection at low MOIs,' indicating the biological significance is uncertain.

results.result: SARS-CoV-2 infection causes widespread downregulation of RNA modifications including m2,2G (~15% decrease at 48 hr) and more than half of all tested RNA modifications at 24 and 48 hr post-infection.
results.evaluation: Reviewer 1 states the authors 'convincingly demonstrate widespread downregulation of RNA modifications during CoV-2 infection.' Reviewer 2 praises 'the authors use state-of-the-art mass spectrometry approach to quantify RNA modifications' and notes they 'demonstrate that several RNA modifications are downregulated during SARS-CoV-2 infection.'

results.result: Nsp5 interacts with TRMT1 through a predicted cleavage site (PRLQ|IANFT, residues 527-534) that matches the consensus sequence of SARS-CoV-2 polyprotein cleavage sites. The catalytically inactive Nsp5-C145A mutant enriches TRMT1 in co-purification experiments.
results.evaluation: Reviewer 1 notes 'they provide solid evidence that TRMT1 is a substrate of Nsp5, revealing an Nsp5 target consensus sequence.' Reviewer 2 states 'the authors go to great lengths to demonstrate that SARS-CoV-2 main protease, Nsp5, interacts and cleaves TRMT1 in cells' and 'the use of an inactive Nsp5 mutant (C145A) strongly supports the claim.'

results.result: Nsp5 cleaves TRMT1 at the predicted Q530 site, generating N-terminal (~58 kDa) and C-terminal (~14 kDa) fragments. The Q530N mutation prevents cleavage by Nsp5.
results.evaluation: Reviewer 1 acknowledges 'evidence of TRMT1 cleavage in cells' but notes 'the detection of the N-terminal TRMT1 fragment by western blot is not robust,' though 'the authors provide corroborating assays and detailed densitometry methods.' Reviewer 2 expresses concern about 'the polyclonal antibody used by the authors shows strong non-specific binding' and 'the cleaved TRMT1 band migrates very closely to a main non-specific band,' though finds 'the loss of this faint cleaved band with the TRMT1 Q530N mutant is reassuring.'

results.result: TRMT1 cleavage fragments exhibit altered RNA binding properties: the N-terminal fragment loses RNA binding ability while the C-terminal fragment containing the zinc-finger motif retains tRNA binding.
results.evaluation: Reviewer 2 states 'the authors rigorously test four protein constructs for their capacity not only to bind RNA but also to introduce the m2,2G modification. They demonstrate that the fragments resulting from TRMT1 cleavage are inactive and cannot methylate RNA. They further establish that the C-terminal region of TRMT1 (containing a zinc-finger domain) is the main binding site for RNA.'

results.result: TRMT1 cleavage fragments are unable to rescue tRNA m2,2G modification in TRMT1-deficient cells, demonstrating that cleavage inactivates TRMT1's enzymatic function.
results.evaluation: Reviewer 1 notes 'theoretically, TRMT1 cleavage should inactivate the modification activity of TRMT1, which the authors thoroughly and elegantly investigate with rigorous biochemical assays.' Reviewer 2 confirms 'the authors rigorously test four protein constructs' and 'demonstrate that the fragments resulting from TRMT1 cleavage are inactive and cannot methylate RNA.'

results.result: TRMT1-deficient cells show reduced SARS-CoV-2 replication, with ~3-4 fold reduction in viral RNA compared to wild-type cells, indicating TRMT1 is necessary for efficient viral replication.
results.evaluation: Reviewer 1 states the authors 'convincingly demonstrate...a requirement for TRMT1 in efficient viral replication.' Reviewer 2 notes 'the authors use two cell lines and well-designed rescue experiments to uncover that TRMT1 is required for optimal SARS-CoV-2 replication,' though cautions that '293T cells are unlikely an ideal model system.'

results.result: During SARS-CoV-2 infection, wild-type TRMT1 levels decrease while the non-cleavable Q530N variant remains stable. Re-expression of TRMT1 rescues viral replication, with Q530N showing enhanced viral RNA production compared to wild-type TRMT1 at higher MOI.
results.evaluation: Reviewer 2 states 'this is an important experiment and unexpectedly reveals that TRMT1 cleavage by Nsp5 is not required for viral replication.' Reviewer 1 notes 'expression of a non-cleavable TRMT1 (versus wild type TRMT1) supports enhanced viral RNA expression at certain MOIs' and that 'TRMT1 cleavage may be an act by CoV-2 to self-limit replication.' However, Reviewer 2 requests the authors 'discuss this in greater detail and its possible implications.'

results.result: TRMT1 expression affects viral particle production and infectivity. TRMT1-KO cells produce viral particles with reduced titer and infectivity, while non-cleavable TRMT1-Q530N enhances both titer and infectivity compared to wild-type TRMT1.
results.evaluation: Reviewer 3 notes 'the discussion on the enhanced viral infectivity upon expression of the non-cleavable TRMT1 is unclear. As presented, this is a bit contradictory to the suggested function of the TRMT1-Nsp5 interaction in diverting the host tRNA pools towards viral propagation.' This indicates confusion about the mechanistic interpretation, though the data itself is not directly challenged.

results.result: Full-length TRMT1 localizes to cytoplasm, nucleus, and mitochondria, while cleavage fragments show altered localization: N-terminal fragment is primarily cytoplasmic, C-terminal fragment is primarily nuclear.
results.evaluation: Reviewer 2 suggests 'cellular Localization experiments of TRMT1 would help clarify' the discrepancy between minor TRMT1 reduction and dramatic m2,2G reduction, noting 'it is possible that TRMT1 is more dramatically degraded in the cytoplasm due to easier access by Nsp5.' The localization data addresses this concern, though no reviewer explicitly evaluates these specific claims.

results.result: The authors conclude that Nsp5-dependent cleavage of TRMT1 and perturbation of tRNA modification patterns contribute to the cellular pathogenesis of SARS-CoV-2 infection.
results.evaluation: The editor states 'the data convincingly support the main conclusions of the paper,' and Reviewer 3 notes 'the authors provide multiple lines of biochemical evidence.' However, Reviewer 1 cautions 'only a minority of TRMT1 undergoes cleavage during infection at low MOIs and thus whether TRMT1 cleavage serves an important functional role during CoV-2 replication will be an important topic for future work.' Reviewer 2 notes 'the cleavage of TRMT1 was dispensable for SARS-CoV-2 replication hinting at the possibility that TRMT1 could be an off-target or fortuitous substrate of Nsp5.'

comparisons.comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C2, C44-C49 regarding Nsp5-TRMT1 interaction and cleavage site identification. Both evaluations find the evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes convergent bioinformatic and biochemical evidence, while peer reviewers highlight the solid evidence for Nsp5 substrate identification and the strength of using inactive Nsp5 mutant.

Perfect agreement on claims C8, C62-C64, C66 regarding RNA binding by TRMT1 fragments. Both evaluations find the evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes the appropriate experimental approach for RNA-protein interactions, while peer reviewers praise the rigorous testing of protein constructs and demonstration that C-terminal region binds RNA.

Perfect agreement on claims C9, C67-C69 regarding functional inactivity of TRMT1 cleavage fragments. Both evaluations find the evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes the appropriate use of TRMT1-KO cells and Q530N controls, while peer reviewers describe the biochemical assays as thorough, elegant, and rigorous.

Perfect agreement on claims C70-C74 regarding TRMT1 localization patterns. Both evaluations find the evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes the distinct localization patterns and appropriate use of markers, while peer reviewers suggest these data help explain the discrepancy between minor bulk TRMT1 reduction and dramatic m2,2G reduction through cytoplasmic-specific degradation.

Both address TRMT1 cleavage evidence (C6, C51-C53, C55-C56, C59-C60). OpenEval finds evidence SUPPORTED with strong site-specificity data, while peer reviewers are UNCERTAIN due to concerns about antibody specificity and weak N-terminal fragment detection, though they find the Q530N control reassuring.

Both address RNA modification changes (C5, C41-C43). OpenEval finds evidence SUPPORTED but notes modest m2,2G reduction (~15%) and broad effects beyond TRMT1. Peer reviewers also find evidence SUPPORTED, praising the state-of-the-art mass spectrometry and convincing demonstration of widespread RNA modification downregulation during infection.

Both address TRMT1 reduction during infection (C4, C40, C118). OpenEval finds evidence SUPPORTED based on quantified immunoblot data and WT vs Q530N comparison. Peer reviewers are UNCERTAIN, noting the reduction is minor in MRC5 cells and only a minority of TRMT1 undergoes cleavage at low MOIs, questioning biological significance.

Both address TRMT1 requirement for viral replication (C10, C78-C79). OpenEval finds evidence SUPPORTED with strong genetic complementation data. Peer reviewers also find evidence SUPPORTED, with Reviewer 1 noting convincing demonstration and Reviewer 2 praising well-designed rescue experiments, though cautioning about 293T cell model limitations.

Partial overlap on TRMT1-Q530N stability and enhanced replication (C75-C77, C80-C81). OpenEval finds evidence SUPPORTED for TRMT1-WT vs Q530N comparison during infection. Peer reviewers also find evidence SUPPORTED, noting this important experiment unexpectedly reveals TRMT1 cleavage is not required for viral replication and may represent viral self-limitation.

Both address viral titer and infectivity with TRMT1 variants (C82-C86). OpenEval finds evidence SUPPORTED but notes unclear mechanism. Peer reviewers are UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 3 finding the enhanced infectivity with non-cleavable TRMT1 contradictory to the suggested function and requesting clearer discussion of implications.

Both address pathogenesis implications (C11, C87). OpenEval finds evidence UNCERTAIN, noting the connection to cellular pathogenesis is speculative given modest m2,2G reduction and that TRMT1-KO reduces viral replication. Peer reviewers are also UNCERTAIN, with concerns that only minority TRMT1 cleavage occurs at low MOIs and TRMT1 could be an off-target substrate.

Minimal overlap on broad RNA modification changes (C109). OpenEval finds evidence SUPPORTED for widespread modification changes but notes mechanisms are not investigated. Peer reviewers also find evidence SUPPORTED, praising the convincing demonstration of widespread RNA modification downregulation using state-of-the-art mass spectrometry.

OpenEval evaluates concurrent independent validation studies (C88-C90) as SUPPORTED corroborating evidence. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific claims about independent validation.

OpenEval evaluates extensive speculative mechanistic claims (C91-C93, C100-C102, C105, C107, C112-C117) as UNCERTAIN, noting they are explicitly speculative and unvalidated. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses this collection of speculative mechanisms, though peer reviewers do request more detailed discussion of implications.
